Ukrainian_National_Democratic_Party.name: Ukrainian National Democratic Party
Ukrainian_National_Democratic_Party.summary: The leading Ukrainian party of Austrian Galicia, founded in 1899; its leaders (Yevhen Petrushevych, Kost Levytsky) dominated the Ukrainian National Rada that proclaimed the West Ukrainian People's Republic in 1918. It was succeeded in the 1920s by the Ukrainian Labour Party and then UNDO.

Ukrainian_Radical_Party.name: Ukrainian Radical Party (Galicia)
Ukrainian_Radical_Party.summary: Founded in 1890 by Ivan Franko and Mykhailo Pavlyk as the first modern Ukrainian political party in Galicia; renamed the Ukrainian Socialist-Radical Party in 1926, it was the second-largest legal Ukrainian party in interwar Poland after UNDO.

Ukrainian_Social_Democratic_Party_(1899).name: Ukrainian Social Democratic Party (Galicia)
Ukrainian_Social_Democratic_Party_(1899).summary: Social-democratic party of Galician and Bukovinian Ukrainians founded in 1899; it took part in the West Ukrainian People's Republic and remained a small force in interwar Poland, running jointly with the Radicals in 1928.

Ukrainian_Socialist-Revolutionary_Party.name: Ukrainian Party of Socialist Revolutionaries
Ukrainian_Socialist-Revolutionary_Party.summary: Peasant-based socialist party that dominated the Central Rada and won the 1917 Constituent Assembly vote in most Ukrainian governorates; its left wing became the Borotbists.

Ukrainian_Social_Democratic_Labour_Party.name: Ukrainian Social Democratic Labour Party
Ukrainian_Social_Democratic_Labour_Party.summary: Party of Volodymyr Vynnychenko and Symon Petliura that led the Central Rada's General Secretariat and later the Directorate of the Ukrainian People's Republic.

Bolsheviks.name: Bolsheviks (RSDLP(b))
Bolsheviks.summary: Lenin's faction of the Russian Social Democratic Labour Party that seized power in Petrograd in November 1917; in Ukraine it organised as the Communist Party (Bolsheviks) of Ukraine from 1918.

Communist_Party_of_Ukraine_(Soviet_Union.name: Communist Party (Bolsheviks) of Ukraine / Communist Party of Ukraine
Communist_Party_of_Ukraine_(Soviet_Union.summary: The Ukrainian branch of the Soviet Communist Party and the sole ruling party of the Ukrainian SSR from 1919/1920 until it was banned after the August 1991 coup attempt; it ruled the western oblasts from 1939/40 and again from 1944.

Hungarian_Communist_Party.name: Party of Communists in Hungary
Hungarian_Communist_Party.summary: Founded in November 1918 under Béla Kun, it led the Hungarian Soviet Republic of March-August 1919, which briefly controlled much of Subcarpathian Ruthenia.

Ukrainian_National_Democratic_Alliance.name: Ukrainian National Democratic Alliance
Ukrainian_National_Democratic_Alliance.summary: The largest legal Ukrainian party in interwar Poland, formed in 1925 and led by Dmytro Levytsky and later Vasyl Mudry; it held Ukrainian seats in the Sejm and Senate, tried a 'normalization' compromise with the Polish government in 1935, and was dissolved after the Soviet annexation in 1939.

Bloc_of_National_Minorities.name: Bloc of National Minorities
Bloc_of_National_Minorities.summary: Electoral alliance of Jewish, Ukrainian, Belarusian and German parties in Poland in the 1922 and 1928 Sejm elections; UNDO and Volhynian Ukrainian groups ran on its lists in 1928.

x:Sel-Rob.name: Sel-Rob (Ukrainian Peasant-Worker Socialist Union)
x:Sel-Rob.summary: Legal left-wing Ukrainian party in Poland (1926-1932), close to the illegal Communist Party of Western Ukraine and strongest in Volhynia and Polesia; it split into Sel-Rob Left and Sel-Rob Right. No dedicated English Wikipedia article; see the 1928 Polish parliamentary election article.

Nonpartisan_Bloc_for_Cooperation_with_th.name: Nonpartisan Bloc for Cooperation with the Government
Nonpartisan_Bloc_for_Cooperation_with_th.summary: Pro-government electoral bloc of Józef Piłsudski's Sanation regime that dominated the Polish Sejm from 1928 and 1930 until its dissolution in 1935.

National_Liberal_Party_(Romania).name: National Liberal Party (Romania)
National_Liberal_Party_(Romania).summary: The dominant Romanian governing party for much of the interwar period, associated with the Brătianu family and a centralising policy toward annexed provinces such as Bukovina.

National_Peasants'_Party.name: National Peasants' Party (Romania)
National_Peasants'_Party.summary: Romanian agrarian party formed in 1926 that governed Romania in 1928-1931 and 1932-1933; it competed with the Liberals for votes in Bukovina.

x:Ukrainian_National_Party_(Bukovina).name: Ukrainian National Party (Bukovina)
x:Ukrainian_National_Party_(Bukovina).summary: Main legal Ukrainian party in Romanian Bukovina (1927-1938), led by Volodymyr Zalozetsky-Sas, which sent a few deputies to the Romanian parliament on alliance lists. No dedicated English Wikipedia article; see Encyclopedia of Ukraine (internetencyclopediaofukraine.com).

Communist_Party_of_Czechoslovakia.name: Communist Party of Czechoslovakia
Communist_Party_of_Czechoslovakia.summary: Founded in 1921, it was the strongest single party in Subcarpathian Ruthenia in several interwar elections, drawing on rural poverty and pro-Soviet sentiment.

Republican_Party_of_Farmers_and_Peasants.name: Republican Party of Farmers and Peasants (Agrarian Party)
Republican_Party_of_Farmers_and_Peasants.summary: The leading governing party of interwar Czechoslovakia; its Subcarpathian branch was one of the main pro-government forces in the region.

Ukrainian_National_Union_(1939).name: Ukrainian National Union
Ukrainian_National_Union_(1939).summary: Unity movement of Avgustyn Voloshyn's autonomous government that ran the single list in the February 1939 Soim election of Carpatho-Ukraine.

x:Autonomous_Agricultural_Union.name: Autonomous Agricultural Union
x:Autonomous_Agricultural_Union.summary: Russophile party of Andrei Brodii and Stepan Fentsyk in Subcarpathian Ruthenia that demanded autonomy and later leaned toward Hungary; Brodii headed the first autonomous government in October 1938. No dedicated English Wikipedia article; see the Encyclopedia of Ukraine.

Communist_Party_of_Transcarpathian_Ukrai.name: Communist Party of Transcarpathian Ukraine
Communist_Party_of_Transcarpathian_Ukrai.summary: Party formed in Mukachevo in November 1944 under Soviet military occupation from the local communists; it ran the provisional Transcarpathian Ukraine and pressed for union with the Ukrainian SSR, merging into the Communist Party of Ukraine in 1946.

Nazi_Party.name: National Socialist German Workers' Party
Nazi_Party.summary: Ruling party of Nazi Germany; its functionaries ran the civil occupation administrations of the District of Galicia (General Government) and the Reichskommissariat Ukraine in 1941-1944.

Unity_Party_(Hungary).name: Party of Hungarian Life (Unity Party)
Unity_Party_(Hungary).summary: Hungary's ruling party under the Horthy regime (renamed Party of Hungarian Life in 1939), which governed Subcarpathia after its reannexation in 1938-1939.

People's_Movement_of_Ukraine.name: People's Movement of Ukraine (Rukh)
People's_Movement_of_Ukraine.summary: Founded in 1989 as a civic movement for perestroika and independence and registered as a party in 1993; it led the Democratic Bloc that won the Galician oblast councils in 1990 under Viacheslav Chornovil.

Ukrainian_Republican_Party.name: Ukrainian Republican Party
Ukrainian_Republican_Party.summary: Successor of the Ukrainian Helsinki Union founded in 1990 by former dissidents such as Levko Lukianenko; it was strong in Galicia in the early 1990s.

Congress_of_Ukrainian_Nationalists.name: Congress of Ukrainian Nationalists
Congress_of_Ukrainian_Nationalists.summary: Party founded in 1992 by the émigré OUN-B under Slava Stetsko, with its base in Galicia.

Our_Ukraine_–_People's_Self-Defense_Bloc.name: Our Ukraine Bloc
Our_Ukraine_–_People's_Self-Defense_Bloc.summary: Viktor Yushchenko's electoral alliance, which won western Ukraine in the 2002 and 2006 elections and backed the Orange Revolution; it ran as Our Ukraine–People's Self-Defense in 2007.

Our_Ukraine_(political_party).name: Our Ukraine (People's Union)
Our_Ukraine_(political_party).summary: Pro-Yushchenko party founded in 2005 on the basis of the Our Ukraine bloc; it lost most support after 2010.

Social_Democratic_Party_of_Ukraine_(unit.name: Social Democratic Party of Ukraine (united)
Social_Democratic_Party_of_Ukraine_(unit.summary: Party associated with Viktor Medvedchuk and the Surkis brothers that was a pillar of President Kuchma's camp; Zakarpattia was one of its strongholds around 1998-2004.

Communist_Party_of_Ukraine.name: Communist Party of Ukraine
Communist_Party_of_Ukraine.summary: Party founded in 1993 as successor to the Soviet-era Communist Party; strong in the east and in rural Podolia in the 1990s, and banned in 2022.

Socialist_Party_of_Ukraine.name: Socialist Party of Ukraine
Socialist_Party_of_Ukraine.summary: Oleksandr Moroz's party, founded in 1991, with a rural base in central and Podolian Ukraine; it joined the Orange coalition in 2004-2006.

Agrarian_Party_of_Ukraine.name: Agrarian Party of Ukraine
Agrarian_Party_of_Ukraine.summary: Rural-interest party (re-founded several times since 1996) that won seats in several western and Podolian oblast councils in 2015 and 2020.

x:KMKS_Party_of_Hungarians_of_Ukraine.name: KMKS – Party of Hungarians of Ukraine
x:KMKS_Party_of_Hungarians_of_Ukraine.summary: Party of the Hungarian minority in Zakarpattia, developed from the Hungarian Cultural Federation of Transcarpathia (KMKSZ) and led by László Brenzovics; it holds seats in the Zakarpattia Oblast Council. No dedicated English Wikipedia article; see the Zakarpattia Oblast Council article.

Democratic_Party_of_Hungarians_of_Ukrain.name: Democratic Party of Hungarians of Ukraine
Democratic_Party_of_Hungarians_of_Ukrain.summary: Hungarian minority party in Zakarpattia associated with the UMDSZ federation and Miklós Kovács, the rival of KMKS.

Yulia_Tymoshenko_Bloc.name: Yulia Tymoshenko Bloc
Yulia_Tymoshenko_Bloc.summary: Yulia Tymoshenko's electoral alliance (2001-2011), the strongest force in central and much of western Ukraine in 2006, built around the Batkivshchyna party.

Batkivshchyna.name: All-Ukrainian Union "Batkivshchyna" (Fatherland)
Batkivshchyna.summary: Yulia Tymoshenko's party founded in 1999; it has won seats in every western oblast council since 2006.

Svoboda_(Ukraine).name: All-Ukrainian Union "Svoboda"
Svoboda_(Ukraine).summary: Nationalist party founded in Lviv in 1991 as the Social-National Party of Ukraine and renamed in 2004 under Oleh Tyahnybok; it won the Ternopil (2009), Lviv (2010) and Ivano-Frankivsk (2010, 2020) councils as the largest party.

Party_of_Regions.name: Party of Regions
Party_of_Regions.summary: Viktor Yanukovych's party, dominant in the east and south (1997-2014); in the west it was strongest in Zakarpattia, Chernivtsi, Rivne and Khmelnytskyi, especially in 2010.

Front_for_Change_(Ukraine).name: Front for Change
Front_for_Change_(Ukraine).summary: Arseniy Yatsenyuk's party (2009-2013), which came second in several western councils in 2010 before merging into Batkivshchyna.

Andriy_Baloha's_Team.name: United Centre / Andriy Baloha's Team
Andriy_Baloha's_Team.summary: Party built by Viktor Baloha, Yushchenko's chief of staff, as United Centre (2008); it dominated the Zakarpattia council in 2010 and 2015 and was renamed Andriy Baloha's Team in 2020.

Ukrainian_People's_Party.name: Ukrainian People's Party
Ukrainian_People's_Party.summary: Rukh splinter party founded in 1999 by Hennadiy Udovenko and later led by Yuriy Kostenko, with its base in Galicia and Volhynia.

Ukrainian_People's_Bloc.name: Ukrainian People's Bloc of Kostenko and Plyushch
Ukrainian_People's_Bloc.summary: Electoral alliance of the Ukrainian People's Party and Ivan Plyushch for the 2006 elections, which won seats in most western oblast councils.

Lytvyn_Bloc.name: Lytvyn Bloc (People's Bloc of Lytvyn)
Lytvyn_Bloc.summary: Electoral alliance around Volodymyr Lytvyn's People's Party, contesting the 2006 and 2007 elections.

People's_Party_(Ukraine).name: People's Party
People's_Party_(Ukraine).summary: Volodymyr Lytvyn's party (formerly the Agrarian Party), which won seats in several western oblast councils in 2010.

PORA.name: PORA
PORA.summary: Youth civic campaign of the Orange Revolution that became a party in 2005 and won seats in the Lviv and Chernivtsi councils in 2006.

Party_of_Industrialists_and_Entrepreneur.name: Party of Industrialists and Entrepreneurs of Ukraine
Party_of_Industrialists_and_Entrepreneur.summary: Business-oriented party founded by Anatoliy Kinakh in 2000, which won seats in the Lviv council in 2006 and 2010.

Strong_Ukraine.name: Strong Ukraine
Strong_Ukraine.summary: Serhiy Tihipko's party, which won small groups of seats in several western councils in 2010 before merging into the Party of Regions in 2012.

Ukrainian_Democratic_Alliance_for_Reform.name: UDAR (Ukrainian Democratic Alliance for Reform)
Ukrainian_Democratic_Alliance_for_Reform.summary: Vitali Klitschko's party, founded in 2010, which later merged with the Petro Poroshenko Bloc.

Revival_(Ukraine).name: Revival (Vidrodzhennia)
Revival_(Ukraine).summary: Party of local business groups that won seats in several western councils in 2010 and 11 seats in Zakarpattia in 2015.

European_Solidarity.name: European Solidarity (Petro Poroshenko Bloc "Solidarity")
European_Solidarity.summary: Petro Poroshenko's party, which ran as the Petro Poroshenko Bloc "Solidarity" in 2014-2015 and won the most seats in most western oblast councils in 2015; renamed European Solidarity in 2019, it again led several western councils in 2020.

Self_Reliance_(political_party).name: Self Reliance (Samopomich)
Self_Reliance_(political_party).summary: Party of Lviv mayor Andriy Sadovyi, founded in 2012, which was strongest in Lviv and Galicia.

Civil_Position.name: Civil Position
Civil_Position.summary: Anatoliy Hrytsenko's party, founded in 2005, which won seats in the Lviv and Ternopil councils in 2015.

UKROP.name: UKROP (Ukrainian Association of Patriots)
UKROP.summary: Party linked to Ihor Kolomoyskyi and Hennadiy Boholiubov that won the most seats in the Volyn council in 2015.

Radical_Party_of_Oleh_Liashko.name: Radical Party of Oleh Liashko
Radical_Party_of_Oleh_Liashko.summary: Populist party of Oleh Liashko founded in 2010 that won seats in most western councils in 2015 and in Rivne and Khmelnytskyi in 2020.

x:People's_Control.name: People's Movement "People's Control"
x:People's_Control.summary: Civic-movement party led by Dmytro Dobrodomov that won seats in the Lviv, Ternopil and Chernivtsi councils in 2015. No English Wikipedia article; see uk.wikipedia.org/wiki/Громадський_рух_«Народний_контроль».

Our_Land_(Ukraine).name: Our Land (Nash Krai)
Our_Land_(Ukraine).summary: Party of former Party of Regions local politicians founded in 2011, which won seats in the Volyn and Chernivtsi councils in 2015.

Opposition_Bloc.name: Opposition Bloc
Opposition_Bloc.summary: Successor alliance of the Party of Regions formed in 2014, which won small groups of seats in Zakarpattia and Chernivtsi in 2015.

x:For_Concrete_Deeds.name: For Concrete Deeds
x:For_Concrete_Deeds.summary: Party of Khmelnytskyi mayor Oleksandr Symchyshyn that won the most seats in the Khmelnytskyi council in 2015. No English Wikipedia article; see uk.wikipedia.org/wiki/За_конкретні_справи.

Liberty_(political_party).name: Volia (Liberty)
Liberty_(political_party).summary: Party around Ivano-Frankivsk politician Yuriy Derevianko that won seats in the Ivano-Frankivsk council in 2015.

Servant_of_the_People.name: Servant of the People
Servant_of_the_People.summary: Volodymyr Zelenskyy's party founded in 2017-2018, which won a parliamentary majority in 2019 but polled more modestly in the 2020 western council elections.

Holos_(Ukraine).name: Holos (Voice)
Holos_(Ukraine).summary: Party founded in 2019 by musician Sviatoslav Vakarchuk, strongest in Lviv.

For_the_Future_(political_party).name: For the Future
For_the_Future_(political_party).summary: Party associated with MP Ihor Palytsia and Ihor Kolomoyskyi's circle that won the most seats in the Volyn council in 2020 and seats in every western council.

Ukrainian_Galician_Party.name: Ukrainian Galician Party
Ukrainian_Galician_Party.summary: Lviv-based regionalist party founded in 2014 that won seats in the Lviv council in 2020.

Strength_and_Honor.name: Strength and Honor
Strength_and_Honor.summary: Party of former security chief Ihor Smeshko, which won seats in the Rivne and Volyn councils in 2020.

Opposition_Platform_–_For_Life.name: Opposition Platform — For Life
Opposition_Platform_–_For_Life.summary: Pro-Russian party of Viktor Medvedchuk and Yuriy Boyko; in the west it won seats only in Zakarpattia and Chernivtsi in 2020, and it was banned in 2022 after the Russian invasion.

Native_Zakarpattia.name: Native Zakarpattia
Native_Zakarpattia.summary: Zakarpattia regional party founded in 2020 that came first in the Zakarpattia council in 2020.

x:United_Alternative.name: United Alternative
x:United_Alternative.summary: Bukovinian regional party that won 9 seats in the Chernivtsi council in 2020. No English Wikipedia article; see the Chernivtsi Oblast Council article.

x:Team_of_Oleksandr_Symchyshyn.name: Team of Oleksandr Symchyshyn
x:Team_of_Oleksandr_Symchyshyn.summary: List of Khmelnytskyi mayor Oleksandr Symchyshyn that tied for first place in the Khmelnytskyi council in 2020. No English Wikipedia article; see the Khmelnytskyi Oblast Council article.

x:Community_Platform.name: Community Platform (Hromadska platforma)
x:Community_Platform.summary: Local party that won 10 seats in the Ivano-Frankivsk council in 2020. No English Wikipedia article; see the Ivano-Frankivsk Oblast Council article.

Dovira.name: Dovira (Trust)
Dovira.summary: Party associated with a group of independent MPs elected in 2019 that won seats in the Ternopil council in 2020.

Liberal_Party_(Hungary).name: Liberal Party (Hungary)
Liberal_Party_(Hungary).summary: Hungary's ruling party from 1875 to 1905, founded by Kálmán Tisza; it governed the Rusyn counties of the Kingdom of Hungary and pursued Magyarization.

Party_of_National_Work.name: National Party of Work
Party_of_National_Work.summary: Hungarian ruling party founded by István Tisza in 1910 as the successor of the Liberal Party, in government until 1917.

x:Indigenous_Autonomous_Party.name: Indigenous Autonomous Party
x:Indigenous_Autonomous_Party.summary: List set up at a meeting of opposition sympathizers in Berehove in February 1924, with Hungarian candidates, for the first election held in Subcarpathian Rus'. No dedicated English Wikipedia article; see the 1924 Užhorod by-election article.

Social_Democratic_Workers'_Party_in_Subc.name: Social Democratic Workers' Party in Subcarpathian Rus'
Social_Democratic_Workers'_Party_in_Subc.summary: Regional social democratic party that ran with the Czechoslovak Social Democrats in the 1924 vote and won one seat.

Carpatho-Russian_Labour_Party_of_Small_P.name: Carpatho-Russian Labour Party of Small Peasants and Landless
Carpatho-Russian_Labour_Party_of_Small_P.summary: Subcarpathian party that contested the 1924 vote in coalition with the Czechoslovak National Social Party and won one seat.

x:Soviet_of_Peasants_Deputies_(Bessarabi.name: Soviet of Peasants' Deputies (Bessarabia)
x:Soviet_of_Peasants_Deputies_(Bessarabi.summary: Peasant list in the 1917 Russian Constituent Assembly election in Bessarabia, which took five of the district's seats. No dedicated English Wikipedia article; see the Bessarabia electoral district article.

Ukrainian_Sich_Riflemen.name: Ukrainian Sich Riflemen
Ukrainian_Sich_Riflemen.type: Volunteer legion of the Austro-Hungarian Army
Ukrainian_Sich_Riflemen.side: Austria-Hungary, then West Ukrainian People's Republic
Ukrainian_Sich_Riflemen.summary: Ukrainian volunteer unit raised in Galicia in 1914; its men led the November 1918 seizure of Lviv and formed the core of the Ukrainian Galician Army.

Ukrainian_Galician_Army.name: Ukrainian Galician Army
Ukrainian_Galician_Army.type: Regular army of the West Ukrainian People's Republic
Ukrainian_Galician_Army.summary: Army of the ZUNR formed in late 1918 that fought Poland in the Polish-Ukrainian War, crossed the Zbruch in July 1919 and then fought alongside the UNR Army against Bolsheviks and Whites.

Ukrainian_People's_Army.name: Ukrainian People's Army (UNR Army)
Ukrainian_People's_Army.type: Regular army of the Ukrainian People's Republic
Ukrainian_People's_Army.summary: Army of the Central Rada and the Directorate (1917-1921) that fought the Bolsheviks, Whites and, in 1919, Poland; it later allied with Poland in 1920.

Polish_Armed_Forces_(Second_Polish_Repub.name: Polish Army (1918-1939)
Polish_Armed_Forces_(Second_Polish_Repub.type: Regular army of the Second Polish Republic
Polish_Armed_Forces_(Second_Polish_Repub.summary: Armed forces of interwar Poland, which defeated the Ukrainian Galician Army in 1918-1919, fought the Polish-Soviet War of 1919-1921 and resisted the German and Soviet invasions of 1939.

Blue_Army_(Poland).name: Blue Army (Haller's Army)
Blue_Army_(Poland).type: Polish expeditionary army formed in France
Blue_Army_(Poland).summary: Polish force formed in France under Józef Haller and sent to Poland in 1919, where it was used against the Ukrainian Galician Army in the decisive Polish offensive of May-July 1919.

Lwów_Eaglets.name: Lwów Eaglets
Lwów_Eaglets.summary: Polish teenagers and students who defended Polish-held quarters of Lviv against the Ukrainian Sich Riflemen in November 1918.

Red_Army.name: Red Army
Red_Army.type: Regular army of Soviet Russia and the USSR
Red_Army.summary: Soviet army that fought the UNR and Poland in 1919-1921, invaded eastern Poland in 1939, and reconquered Ukraine from the Axis in 1943-1944.

1st_Cavalry_Army.name: 1st Cavalry Army (Budyonny's Konarmiya)
1st_Cavalry_Army.summary: Semyon Budyonny's cavalry army, which swept through Volhynia and attacked Lviv in summer 1920 before defeat at Komarów.

Romanian_Land_Forces.name: Romanian Army
Romanian_Land_Forces.summary: Romanian forces occupied Bukovina in November 1918 and Pokuttia in 1919, and in 1941-1944 occupied Northern Bukovina and Transnistria as Germany's ally.

Czechoslovak_Army.name: Czechoslovak Army
Czechoslovak_Army.summary: Czechoslovak forces took Subcarpathian Ruthenia from Hungary in 1919 and garrisoned it until withdrawing in March 1939.

Hungarian_Ground_Forces.name: Hungarian Red Army
Hungarian_Ground_Forces.type: Army of the Hungarian Soviet Republic
Hungarian_Ground_Forces.summary: Army of Béla Kun's Soviet Republic (March-August 1919), which fought Czechoslovak and Romanian troops in Subcarpathia. The Wikipedia link points to the general article on Hungarian ground forces.

Royal_Hungarian_Honvéd.name: Royal Hungarian Honvéd
Royal_Hungarian_Honvéd.type: Regular army of the Kingdom of Hungary
Royal_Hungarian_Honvéd.summary: Hungarian army that invaded Carpatho-Ukraine in March 1939, took part in the 1941 invasion of the USSR, and held the Árpád Line in the Carpathians until autumn 1944.

Carpathian_Sich.name: Carpathian Sich
Carpathian_Sich.summary: Paramilitary organisation of Carpatho-Ukraine formed in 1938 with OUN volunteers from Galicia; it fought the Hungarian invasion in March 1939.

Ukrainian_Military_Organization.name: Ukrainian Military Organization
Ukrainian_Military_Organization.summary: Clandestine organisation founded in 1920 by Ukrainian Galician Army veterans under Yevhen Konovalets that carried out sabotage and assassinations against Polish rule; it merged into the OUN in 1929.

Organisation_of_Ukrainian_Nationalists.name: Organisation of Ukrainian Nationalists
Organisation_of_Ukrainian_Nationalists.summary: Founded in 1929; its underground waged a campaign of sabotage and assassinations in interwar Poland and, after its 1940 split, the Bandera faction created the UPA and the Melnyk faction worked with the German authorities.

Ukrainian_Insurgent_Army.name: Ukrainian Insurgent Army
Ukrainian_Insurgent_Army.summary: Insurgent army formed in Volhynia in 1942-1943 by OUN-B that fought German occupation forces, Soviet partisans and the Polish underground, carried out the massacres of Poles in Volhynia and Eastern Galicia, and waged a guerrilla war against Soviet rule until the early 1950s.

Ukrainian_People's_Revolutionary_Army.name: Ukrainian People's Revolutionary Army (Polissian Sich)
Ukrainian_People's_Revolutionary_Army.summary: Partisan force of Taras Bulba-Borovets in Polesia and Volhynia (1941-1943) that was forcibly absorbed or disarmed by OUN-B in 1943.

Home_Army.name: Home Army (Armia Krajowa)
Home_Army.summary: Main Polish resistance force in WWII; in Volhynia its 27th Infantry Division and self-defence posts fought the UPA in 1943-1944, and in July 1944 it rose in Lviv during Operation Tempest before the Soviets disarmed it.

14th_Waffen_Grenadier_Division_of_the_SS.name: 14th Waffen Grenadier Division of the SS (1st Galician)
14th_Waffen_Grenadier_Division_of_the_SS.summary: Division recruited from Galician Ukrainians in 1943 with the backing of the Ukrainian Central Committee; it was largely destroyed at Brody in July 1944.

Nachtigall_Battalion.name: Nachtigall Battalion
Nachtigall_Battalion.type: Abwehr special unit of Ukrainian volunteers
Nachtigall_Battalion.summary: Battalion of Ukrainian nationalists under German command that entered Lviv on 30 June 1941, the day OUN-B proclaimed Ukrainian statehood there.

Ukrainian_Auxiliary_Police.name: Ukrainian Auxiliary Police
Ukrainian_Auxiliary_Police.summary: Local police formed under German occupation in 1941 that took part in the Holocaust; in spring 1943 thousands of its members in Volhynia deserted to the UPA.

Wehrmacht.name: Wehrmacht
Wehrmacht.summary: German armed forces that invaded Poland in 1939 and the USSR in June 1941 and held western Ukraine until 1944.

Soviet_partisans.name: Soviet partisans
Soviet_partisans.summary: Pro-Soviet guerrilla units directed from Moscow; in the west they were active in the Volhynian and Polesian forests, and Sydir Kovpak's formation raided the Carpathians in summer 1943.

NKVD.name: NKVD / MGB internal troops
NKVD.type: Soviet security police and internal troops
NKVD.summary: Soviet security apparatus responsible for arrests and deportations in 1939-1941, the June 1941 prison massacres, and the counter-insurgency campaign against the UPA in 1944-1954.

Extermination_battalion.name: Destruction (extermination) battalions
Extermination_battalion.summary: NKVD-controlled local militias (istrebitelnye batalyony), used extensively in western Ukraine in 1944-1954 against the UPA underground.

Carpathian_Military_District.name: Carpathian Military District
Carpathian_Military_District.summary: Military district headquartered in Lviv (1946-1991) covering western Ukraine, one of the Soviet army's main frontline districts facing NATO; it became the Ukrainian Western Operational Command in 1992-1998.

13th_Army_(Soviet_Union).name: 13th Army (Soviet Union)
13th_Army_(Soviet_Union).summary: Combined-arms army headquartered in Rivne in the Carpathian Military District after WWII; its units passed to Ukraine in 1991-1992.

38th_Army_(Soviet_Union).name: 38th Army (Soviet Union)
38th_Army_(Soviet_Union).summary: Combined-arms army headquartered in Ivano-Frankivsk in the Carpathian Military District, covering the Carpathian and Transcarpathian region.

43rd_Rocket_Army.name: 43rd Rocket Army
43rd_Rocket_Army.summary: Strategic missile army headquartered in Vinnytsia whose divisions included the 19th Rocket Division near Khmelnytskyi; its silos were dismantled after Ukraine gave up nuclear weapons.

Operational_Command_West.name: Operational Command West
Operational_Command_West.summary: Successor of the Soviet Carpathian Military District, headquartered in Lviv (as Western Operational Command, later Operational Command West), responsible for the western oblasts.

Ukrainian_National_Assembly_–_Ukrainian_.name: UNA-UNSO
Ukrainian_National_Assembly_–_Ukrainian_.summary: Far-right party and paramilitary founded in 1990-1991 with roots in Lviv; its volunteers fought in Transnistria, Abkhazia and Chechnya in the 1990s.

24th_Mechanized_Brigade_(Ukraine).name: 24th Mechanized Brigade "King Danylo"
24th_Mechanized_Brigade_(Ukraine).summary: Brigade based at Yavoriv in Lviv Oblast that has fought in Donbas since 2014 and on the eastern front since 2022.

80th_Air_Assault_Brigade.name: 80th Air Assault Brigade
80th_Air_Assault_Brigade.summary: Lviv-based air assault brigade that fought at Luhansk airport in 2014 and in the Donbas, Kharkiv and Kursk campaigns after 2022.

128th_Mountain_Assault_Brigade.name: 128th Mountain Assault Brigade

The Radicals (1890), National Democrats (1899) and Social Democrats (1899) all formed here and competed with Russophiles for Ukrainian voters; in 1908 the student Myroslav Sichynsky assassinated Viceroy Andrzej Potocki in Lviv in protest at the electoral system.

Polish forces retook the city within three weeks, so the ZUNR government sat in Ternopil and Stanislaviv; by July 1919 Poland controlled all of Eastern Galicia. Galicia was under Austria and did not vote in the 1917 Russian Constituent Assembly election.

Polish youth volunteers held the western quarters of Lviv in November 1918 until Polish relief troops arrived.

Polish troops broke the siege of Lviv and pushed the Ukrainian forces east in 1919.
Haller's army spearheaded the May 1919 offensive that drove the Galician Army out of the Lviv region.

politics.note: The area was under Polish military and then civil administration after July 1919; the Entente recognised Polish sovereignty over Eastern Galicia only in 1923. In summer 1920 the Red Army tried to take Lviv, and a short-lived Galician Soviet Socialist Republic was proclaimed in Ternopil, but it never controlled the city.

This region lay outside the USSR and did not experience the Holodomor.

The Communist Party then ruled Lviv and Drohobych oblasts, dissolving all Polish and Ukrainian parties, including UNDO.

armedGroups.role: Polish troops defended Lviv against German and then Soviet forces in September 1939.

The NKVD deported tens of thousands and killed several thousand prisoners in Lviv's prisons in June 1941.
The OUN, which split in 1940, kept an underground in Lviv that the NKVD repeatedly hunted.

politics.note: On 30 June 1941 OUN-B proclaimed a Ukrainian state in Lviv; the Germans arrested its leaders and from August 1941 ran the area as the District of Galicia of the General Government under NSDAP officials. The Ukrainian Central Committee acted as a German-permitted welfare body. The Holocaust destroyed Lviv's large Jewish community.

armedGroups.role: The battalion entered Lviv with German troops on 30 June 1941.
Local police served the German administration in Lviv and took part in anti-Jewish actions.

UPA units operated in the Lviv region's forests from 1943-1944.
The Home Army rose in Lviv in July 1944 during Operation Tempest and was then disarmed by the Soviets.
The Red Army retook Lviv on 27 July 1944 in the Lvov-Sandomierz offensive.

armedGroups.role: The UPA and OUN underground fought Soviet rule in the Lviv region until the early 1950s; commander Roman Shukhevych was killed near Lviv in 1950.
NKVD/MGB troops ran counter-insurgency sweeps and mass deportations such as Operation West in October 1947.
Local destruction battalions were raised in villages to fight the nationalist underground.

Seat totals for 1990 are not available on Wikipedia.

In May 1919 the Central Ruthenian National Council in Uzhhorod accepted union with Czechoslovakia. The region did not vote in the 1917 Russian Constituent Assembly election.

politics.note: Communist Party rule continued until 1991. Seat totals for the 1990 council election are not available on Wikipedia.

armedGroups.role: The 43rd Rocket Army's 19th Rocket Division had intercontinental missile silos near Khmelnytskyi.
The oblast's garrisons, including the Starokostiantyniv airbase, were in the Carpathian Military District.

politics.note: Left-wing and agrarian parties (the Communist and Socialist parties) were strong in rural Podolia in the 1990s, while Our Ukraine led in 2002; regional state administrations were headed by presidential appointees. Council seat breakdowns for 1994-2002 are not available on Wikipedia.

armedGroups.role: The missile silos near Khmelnytskyi were dismantled in the 1990s after Ukraine gave up its nuclear arsenal.
The Su-24 bomber unit was based at Starokostiantyniv.

politics.note: The Yulia Tymoshenko Bloc led the council elected in 2006 (with Our Ukraine's Ivan Hladuniak as chair); in 2010 the Party of Regions won the most seats under the mixed system and Mykola Derykot chaired the council. The 2010 figures add the list and constituency seats given in the source.

armedGroups.role: The bomber brigade at Starokostiantyniv was the oblast's main military unit.

politics.note: Mayor Oleksandr Symchyshyn's For Concrete Deeds came first in 2015; in 2020 his Team and For the Future tied for first place. Regional state administrations were headed by presidential appointees.

armedGroups.role: The Starokostiantyniv Su-24 bombers flew combat missions over Donbas in 2014.

politics.note: Under martial law the 2020 council continued and executive power passed to the oblast military administration; elections were suspended.

armedGroups.role: Russian missiles and drones repeatedly struck the Starokostiantyniv airbase and, in May 2023, set off large explosions at a military depot in Khmelnytskyi.
From 2023 the brigade's Su-24s launched Storm Shadow and SCALP cruise missiles.
Khmelnytskyi's territorial defence brigade was raised in 2022 and later deployed east.

politics.note: The 2020 council and the military administration continued under martial law.

armedGroups.role: Russia kept targeting Starokostiantyniv and the oblast's energy infrastructure, near the Khmelnytskyi Nuclear Power Plant.
The brigade continued cruise-missile strikes on Russian-held targets.

politics.note: Elections remained suspended under martial law; the 2020 council and military administration continued.

armedGroups.role: Russian strikes on Starokostiantyniv and Khmelnytskyi continued.
The brigade continued to serve on the front.
